mainTopic: The יפת תואר's mourning, keeping uncircumcised slaves according to רבי עקיבא, and why converts suffer
overview: The amud opens by finishing the פסוק about the יפת תואר. רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue whether 'her father and her mother' means her real parents or her idols. The תנא קמא and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר then argue whether she waits thirty or ninety days, and רבינא's challenge to the ninety-day count stays unanswered. Next comes a ברייתא in which רבי ישמעאל allows keeping uncircumcised slaves and רבי עקיבא forbids it. They argue over the פסוק 'וינפש בן אמתך', which another ברייתא shows is about an uncircumcised slave. The גמרא then shows that even רבי עקיבא allows some cases: a slave who has not firmly refused מילה may be kept up to twelve months, and so may a slave bought on condition not to be circumcised. רבי עקיבא simply named one of several valid cases. A story about a city that waited twelve months before selling its slaves is traced to a ברייתא, where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagrees. Finally, a ברייתא gives four reasons why converts suffer, ending with a פסוק from רות.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: her real parents
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads 'her father and her mother' literally, as the captive woman's actual parents.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: 'Her father' means her real father, and 'her mother' means her real mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אליעזר's explanation of whom the יפת תואר cries for: her actual parents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says she cries for 'her father and her mother.' רבי אליעזר takes the words at face value. She is mourning the family she was taken away from.

keyTerms.meaning: A beautiful captive woman taken in war, whom the תורה allows a soldier to marry after a process

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"Her father" means her actual father,
phrases.notes: This is from the פסוק about the captive woman crying for her parents, דברים 21:13.

phrases.english: "her mother" means her actual mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the יפת תואר פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Her father and her mother' means her real parents.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: her father and mother are the idol
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says 'her father and her mother' means the עבודה זרה she used to worship, and brings a פסוק from ירמיהו as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'Her father and her mother' is idol worship. And so the פסוק says: 'They say to a tree: You are my father,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי אליעזר and says she is crying over the idols she can no longer serve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא shows that idol worshippers really do call their idols 'father' and 'mother'. A פסוק in ירמיהו describes people telling a tree 'you are my father' and a stone 'you gave birth to us'. So 'her father and her mother' can mean the idols she is giving up.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says, introducing a supporting פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
"Her father and her mother": this is idol worship.
And so it says:
"They say to a tree: You are my father," and so on.
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 2:27. The rest of the פסוק has them telling a stone, 'you gave birth to us.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same words רבי אליעזר explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Her father and her mother' refers to the idols she worshipped, supported by ירמיהו 2:27.

steps.title: A month of days means thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion explains 'a month of days' as one thirty-day month.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A month of days' means a month of thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to how long the יפת תואר waits, and the first opinion says thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says she cries 'a month of days' and only after that may the soldier marry her. This opinion reads 'a month of days' as one full month of thirty days.

phrases.english: "A month of days" means a month of thirty days.
phrases.notes: דברים 21:13. The פסוק goes on, 'and after that you may come to her.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who she cries for to how long she waits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waiting period is thirty days.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: ninety days
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says she waits ninety days, counting thirty for each of three phrases in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: ninety days. 'A month' is thirty, 'days' is another thirty, and 'after that' is another thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagrees and stretches the waiting time to ninety days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He finds a thirty-day period in three separate words. 'Month' is thirty. The extra word 'days' adds another thirty. 'And after that' means one more period of the same length, so another thirty.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר, תִּשְׁעִים יוֹם:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: ninety days:
"A month" is thirty, "days" is thirty,
"and after that" is thirty.
phrases.notes: He reads 'after that' as one more stretch the same length as the one before it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר, תִּשְׁעִים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with the thirty-day opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waiting period is ninety days: thirty for each of the three phrases.

steps.title: רבינא: why not sixty for 'after that'?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks why 'after that' adds only thirty days. Perhaps it should equal both earlier periods together, which is sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenges this: Say instead that 'a month' is thirty, 'days' is thirty, and 'after that' is as much as both of these together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges how רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reads the words 'and after that'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'after that' means another period equal to what came before, then what came before is sixty days, not thirty. That would make the total 120 days. So the ninety-day count seems to have no clear basis.

keyTerms.meaning: Like these (equal to both of them)

phrases.english: Ravina strongly objects to this:
Say: "a month" is thirty, "days" is thirty,
and "after that" is like these?
phrases.notes: He means equal to both earlier periods together, so sixty more days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's reading in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's reading of 'and after that' as only thirty more days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'after that' means 'equal to what came before,' then what came before is sixty days, so it should add sixty.

steps.title: The question stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that רבינא's challenge is difficult and gives no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that רבינא's question is strong and leaves it unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' on its own means the challenge stands and has no answer. The reading of 'after that' as thirty days stays a weak point in רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the challenge stands unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says the יפת תואר waits thirty days and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says ninety. רבינא's question on the ninety-day reading is left without an answer.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' at the end does not mean the opinion is thrown out completely. It only means this particular question was not answered.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion by admitting רבינא's question stands.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבינא's challenge to the ninety-day reading remains unanswered.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: you may keep uncircumcised slaves
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל allows an owner to keep slaves who are not circumcised.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may keep slaves who are not circumcised. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about keeping a non-Jewish slave who has not had a ברית מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a Jew's slave is supposed to be circumcised. רבי ישמעאל says the owner may still keep a slave who is not circumcised in his house.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may keep slaves that are not circumcised,
this is the statement of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְקַיְּימִין עֲבָדִים שֶׁאֵינָם מָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is permitted to keep uncircumcised slaves.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: you may not keep them
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא forbids keeping uncircumcised slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: One may not keep them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל and says an uncircumcised slave may not be kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up a clear מחלוקת. רבי ישמעאל permits keeping the slave and רבי עקיבא forbids it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: One may not keep them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי ישמעאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to keep uncircumcised slaves.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's proof from the שבת פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל challenges רבי עקיבא from the פסוק that commands rest on שבת for 'the son of your maidservant'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said to him: But the פסוק says: 'And the son of your maidservant will rest.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל brings a פסוק to show that the תורה expects a Jew to have uncircumcised slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires the owner to let 'the son of your maidservant' rest on שבת. רבי ישמעאל understands this as a slave who is not circumcised. If the תורה gives a rule about such a slave, it must be allowed to keep him.

keyTerms.meaning: But it says, a challenge from a פסוק
And he will rest, be refreshed

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said to him:
But it says:
"And the son of your maidservant will be refreshed"!
phrases.notes: שמות 23:12. This is about letting him rest on שבת. רבי ישמעאל takes it as a slave who isn't circumcised.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי ישמעאל attacks רבי עקיבא's view with a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling that uncircumcised slaves may not be kept.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה gives a שבת rule for an uncircumcised slave, so keeping such a slave must be allowed.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a slave bought just before שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that the פסוק is about a slave bought at twilight before שבת, when there was no time to circumcise him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The פסוק is talking about someone who bought a slave at twilight and did not have time to circumcise him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers the challenge by limiting the פסוק to one unusual case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא agrees that the פסוק is about an uncircumcised slave. He says it only describes a short gap that could not be avoided: the slave was bought right before שבת, and the owner could not circumcise him in time. The פסוק does not allow keeping such a slave long-term.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, the time between sunset and nightfall
The פסוק is speaking (about this case)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל allows keeping uncircumcised slaves and רבי עקיבא forbids it. רבי עקיבא explains that the שבת פסוק is only about a slave bought too late on ערב שבת to be circumcised.

phrases.english: He said to him:
About one who buys a slave at twilight
phrases.notes: Twilight on ערב שבת, right before שבת begins.

phrases.english: and did not have time to circumcise him
the verse is speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: בְּלוֹקֵחַ עֶבֶד בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ישמעאל's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the פסוק to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to show that one may keep uncircumcised slaves in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only covers a slave bought at twilight before שבת, when there was no time to circumcise him.

steps.title: Everyone agrees the פסוק speaks about an uncircumcised slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא agree that 'וינפש בן אמתך' refers to an uncircumcised slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, everyone agrees that 'and the son of your maidservant will be refreshed' is written about an uncircumcised slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls out the one point both sides of the argument share: the פסוק is talking about a slave who is not circumcised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל used the פסוק to show you may keep an uncircumcised slave. רבי עקיבא limited it to a slave bought at twilight before שבת. Either way, both read the פסוק as describing an uncircumcised slave.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone, meaning all the opinions in the argument
A slave who is not circumcised

phrases.english: In any event, according to everyone,
phrases.notes: He means both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא from the steps just before.

phrases.english: "And the son of your maidservant will be refreshed"
phrases.notes: שמות 23:12

phrases.english: is written about an uncircumcised slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the shared assumption behind רבי ישמעאל's question and רבי עקיבא's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both opinions read 'וינפש בן אמתך' as speaking about an uncircumcised slave.

steps.title: How do we know the פסוק means an uncircumcised slave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source showing that the פסוק refers to an uncircumcised slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of the point it just made. It is setting up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words 'בן אמתך' do not say anything about מילה. So the גמרא wants to know what tells us this slave is uncircumcised.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is this understood? What shows this?

phrases.english: From where is this understood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the claim in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The textual source showing that 'וינפש בן אמתך' speaks of an uncircumcised slave.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves it from a second פסוק about slaves resting
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that a circumcised slave is already covered by a different פסוק, so 'וינפש בן אמתך' must be about an uncircumcised slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And the son of your maidservant will be refreshed' speaks about an uncircumcised slave. You say uncircumcised, but maybe it means a circumcised slave? Since another פסוק says 'so that your slave and your maidservant may rest like you,' the circumcised slave is already mentioned. So how do I explain 'and the son of your maidservant will be refreshed'? It must mean an uncircumcised slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. There are two פסוקים about slaves resting on שבת, so each one must be teaching about a different kind of slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים, 'like you,' describes a slave who is like a Jew: a circumcised slave. The תורה does not repeat itself for nothing, so the second פסוק in שמות must add a new case, the uncircumcised slave.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain this פסוק? What is it for?

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that an uncircumcised slave can belong to a Jew and still be included in the מצוה of שבת rest. That is the basis for the argument about keeping such a slave.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And the son of your maidservant will be refreshed"
the verse is speaking about an uncircumcised slave.
Do you say it is about an uncircumcised slave,
or perhaps it is only about a circumcised slave?
When it says
"so that your slave and your maidservant may rest like you,"
phrases.notes: דברים 5:14

phrases.english: a circumcised slave is already mentioned.
So how do I explain
"And the son of your maidservant will be refreshed"?
It is about an uncircumcised slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12's question with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since 'like you' in דברים already covers a circumcised slave, 'וינפש בן אמתך' must be about an uncircumcised slave.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: 'והגר' means a גר תושב
steps.stepSummary: Using the same method, the ברייתא shows that 'והגר' in the same פסוק refers to a גר תושב, since a גר צדק is already mentioned elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the stranger': this is a גר תושב. You say a גר תושב, but maybe it means a גר צדק? Since another פסוק says 'and your stranger who is within your gates,' a גר צדק is already mentioned. So how do I explain 'and the stranger'? It is a גר תושב.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going with the next words of the same פסוק and uses the exact same pattern of reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים lists 'your stranger' along with the Jewish household, so it means a full convert, a גר צדק. The extra 'והגר' in שמות must then teach about a גר תושב, a non-Jew who keeps certain מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew who accepts certain מצוות and lives among Jews, but has not fully converted
Within your gates, in your town

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of גר. A גר צדק is fully Jewish. A גר תושב is still a non-Jew, even though he keeps some מצוות.

phrases.english: "And the stranger"
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק, שמות 23:12.

phrases.english: this is a ger toshav.
Do you say this is a ger toshav,
or perhaps it is only a righteous convert?
When it says
"and your stranger who is within your gates,"
phrases.notes: דברים 5:14

phrases.english: a righteous convert is already mentioned.
So how do I explain
"And the stranger"?
This is a ger toshav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same ברייתא goes on to the next words of the פסוק using the same reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'והגר' in שמות 23:12 refers to a גר תושב, because a גר צדק is already covered by 'וגרך אשר בשעריך'.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: try for twelve months, then sell him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that if a slave bought from a gentile refuses מילה, the owner may keep working with him for up to twelve months. If he still refuses, the owner sells him back to gentiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: If someone buys a slave from a gentile and the slave does not want to be circumcised, the owner keeps trying with him for up to twelve months. If he still has not circumcised, the owner sells him back to gentiles.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא teaches a practical rule about a slave who refuses מילה. The owner may keep him for a limited time, up to a year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule allows keeping an uncircumcised slave for a while, but not forever. After twelve months of refusal, the owner must get rid of him by selling him to non-Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeps working with him, keeps trying to convince him

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical time limit for keeping an uncircumcised slave, and it leads straight into the question of whether it fits רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One who buys a slave from a gentile
and the slave did not want to be circumcised,

phrases.aramaic: מְגַלְגֵּל עִמּוֹ עַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: he keeps going along with him for up to twelve months.
phrases.notes: Literally 'rolls along with him.' He keeps him around and keeps trying to persuade him.

phrases.english: If he still did not get circumcised,
he goes back and sells him to gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a practical אמורא ruling on the same topic of keeping uncircumcised slaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave bought from a gentile who refuses מילה may be kept up to twelve months. After that he must be sold to gentiles.

steps.title: The רבנן ask: this can't fit רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say before רב פפא that רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule seems to go against רבי עקיבא, who forbids keeping an uncircumcised slave at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said this rule before רב פפא: Whose opinion is it? Not רבי עקיבא's. Because if it were רבי עקיבא, didn't he say one may not keep an uncircumcised slave?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge the rule: twelve months of keeping an uncircumcised slave seems to clash with רבי עקיבא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said 'אין מקיימין,' you may not keep an uncircumcised slave. רבי יהושע בן לוי allows keeping him for up to a year. So it looks like his rule only works according to רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, in front of him
According to whom? Whose opinion is this?
One may not keep (an uncircumcised slave)

phrases.english: The Rabbis said this teaching before Rav Pappa:
According to whom is it?
It must be not like Rabbi Akiva.
For if it were Rabbi Akiva, didn't he say:
One may not keep him!
phrases.notes: This is רבי עקיבא's opinion from step 8.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא, כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule from step 15 using רבי עקיבא's opinion in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's twelve-month rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא forbids keeping an uncircumcised slave, so allowing it for twelve months seems to contradict him.

steps.title: רב פפא: רבי עקיבא forbids it only when the slave firmly refused
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the rule can fit רבי עקיבא. The twelve months apply when the slave has not firmly refused. Once he firmly refuses, he may not be kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to them: You can even say this is רבי עקיבא. That rule applies where the slave did not make his refusal final. But where he did make it final, it is final, and he may not be kept.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends the rule by splitting the cases. The twelve months are for a slave who has not given a final no. רבי עקיבא's ban is for a slave who has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real contradiction, because the two rules talk about different situations. A slave who has not clearly refused may still agree, so the owner can keep trying. A slave who has clearly refused may not be kept at all, even according to this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He made his decision final, gave a clear answer

steps.whatToRemember: A slave who refuses מילה may be kept up to twelve months only if he has not firmly refused. Once he clearly refuses, even רבי עקיבא's opinion fits: he may not be kept.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to them:
You can even say it follows Rabbi Akiva,
since that rule applies where
he did not make his refusal final;
but where he did make his refusal final,
he has made it final, and he may not be kept.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by limiting each rule to a different case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each rule applies to a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule clashes with רבי עקיבא's ban, so it must follow רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The twelve months apply only when the slave has not firmly refused. רבי עקיבא's ban applies once he firmly refuses, so the rule fits רבי עקיבא too.

steps.title: רב זביד asks why רבי עקיבא didn't use this case
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports that רב זביד challenged רב פפא's answer. If רבי עקיבא allows keeping a slave who has not firmly refused, he should have given that case to רבי ישמעאל, not the 'bought at twilight' case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I told this teaching to רב זביד from נהרדעא. He said to me: If that is so, then when רבי עקיבא told רבי ישמעאל that the פסוק is about someone who buys a slave at twilight, he should have answered him with this case instead!
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד attacks רב פפא's answer from step 17. He points out that רבי עקיבא, in his own argument with רבי ישמעאל, never mentioned the 'not firmly refused' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי עקיבא explained the פסוק about an uncircumcised slave as a slave bought right before שבת, who could not yet be circumcised. If רבי עקיבא also allowed keeping a slave who had not firmly refused, that would have been an easier example. His silence suggests he does not really allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: I said the teaching (I repeated the ruling)
Twilight, the unclear time between day and night

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
I said this teaching
phrases.notes: He means רבי יהושע בן לוי's twelve-month rule, together with רב פפא's explanation from the last step.

phrases.english: before Rav Zevid from Neharde'a.
He said to me: If so,
when Rabbi Akiva said to him
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי ישמעאל, who argued with רבי עקיבא about this פסוק earlier on the דף.

phrases.english: that it is about one who buys a slave at twilight,
let him answer him with this!
phrases.notes: 'This' means the case of a slave who has not firmly refused מילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כִּי אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּלוֹקֵחַ עֶבֶד בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת, לִישַׁנֵּי לֵיהּ הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer that רבי עקיבא agrees to the twelve-month rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that רבי עקיבא allows keeping a slave who has not firmly refused
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי עקיבא agreed, he would have used this simpler case in his answer to רבי ישמעאל. Since he did not, he must not agree.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא gave only one of two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא mentioned just one of the two possible cases. He did not have to list them all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said one out of two reasons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב זביד. רבי עקיבא picked one example, and that does not mean he rejects the other one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving a case out does not prove someone disagrees with it. Both the twilight case and the 'not firmly refused' case are valid, and רבי עקיבא just mentioned one of them. So רב פפא's answer still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that if a תנא gives one example, he rejects every other example. Often he just picks one.

phrases.english: He said one out of two reasons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב זביד's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Leaving a case out is not a rejection; the תנא listed only one of several valid reasons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's silence about the 'not firmly refused' case shows he forbids it
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא gave one example out of two, so he can still agree with the twelve-month rule

steps.title: A slave bought on condition not to be circumcised may be kept
steps.stepSummary: רבין sends a ruling in the name of רבי אילעאי. The uncircumcised slave one may keep is one whose master bought him on condition not to circumcise him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין sent a message in the name of רבי אילעאי, and all my teachers told me this in his name: Which uncircumcised slave may be kept? One whose master bought him on condition that he would not circumcise him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about a different kind of uncircumcised slave that may be kept. This is the slave bought with a condition that he stays uncircumcised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the cases were a slave bought at twilight and a slave who has not firmly refused. Now a third case is added: the slave agreed ahead of time, as part of the sale, not to be circumcised.

phrases.english: Ravin sent in the name of Rabbi Ilai,
and all my teachers told me in his name:
Which is the uncircumcised slave
that one is allowed to keep?
This is one whose master bought him
on condition not to circumcise him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ruling about another uncircumcised slave that may be kept
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave bought on condition that he will not be circumcised may be kept uncircumcised

steps.title: The רבנן say this goes against רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רב פפא that רבי אילעאי's ruling seems not to fit רבי עקיבא, who says an uncircumcised slave may not be kept at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said this before רב פפא: Whose view is this? It is not רבי עקיבא's, because רבי עקיבא said: One may not keep an uncircumcised slave!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge the new ruling. They say it clashes with רבי עקיבא's strict position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as step 16, now aimed at the condition case. רבי עקיבא said not to keep an uncircumcised slave at all, so allowing one because of a condition seems to go against him.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said it before Rav Pappa:
Like whom? Not like Rabbi Akiva,
for if it were Rabbi Akiva, didn't he say:
One may not keep him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אילעאי's ruling from step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעאי's ruling allowing a slave bought on condition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא forbids keeping any uncircumcised slave, so this ruling cannot match his view

steps.title: רב פפא: a condition makes the difference even for רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that רבי עקיבא's ban applies only when no condition was made. If the master made a condition, it works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to them: You can even say this fits רבי עקיבא. His ban applies when the master did not make a condition with the slave. But where he did make a condition, the condition counts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends the ruling. He limits רבי עקיבא's ban to a slave bought without any condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's 'one may not keep' is about a regular purchase. When the slave was bought with a clear agreement not to be circumcised, that agreement holds, and even רבי עקיבא would allow keeping him.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to them:
You can even say it is Rabbi Akiva,
his words apply where
he did not make a condition with him,
but where he made a condition,
he made a condition.
phrases.notes: He means the condition counts, so the slave may be kept.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא אַתְנִי בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits רבי עקיבא's ban to a purchase made without a condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא forbids every uncircumcised slave, even one bought with a condition
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא's ban applies only without a condition. When a condition was made, he agrees the slave may be kept.

steps.title: רב זביד asks the same question about the condition case
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד challenges again. If רבי עקיבא allows the condition case, he should have answered רבי ישמעאל with it instead of the twilight case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I told this teaching to רב זביד from נהרדעא, and he said to me: If so, then when רבי עקיבא told רבי ישמעאל that the פסוק is about someone who buys a slave at twilight and has no time to circumcise him, he should have answered him with this case instead!
steps.whatsHappening: The same challenge from step 18 comes back, now against רב פפא's answer about the condition case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי עקיבא allowed keeping a slave bought on condition, that would have been a clear example for the פסוק. His choice of the twilight case suggests he does not allow the condition case.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
I said this teaching
phrases.notes: This time he means רבי אילעאי's ruling about the condition, with רב פפא's explanation.

phrases.english: before Rav Zevid from Neharde'a,
and he said to me: If so,
when Rabbi Akiva said to him
that it is about one who buys a slave at twilight
and did not have time to circumcise him,
let him answer him with this!
phrases.notes: 'This' is the slave bought on condition not to be circumcised.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כִּי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּלוֹקֵחַ עֶבֶד בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת וְלֹא הִסְפִּיק לְמוּלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer from step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that רבי עקיבא allows the condition case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא would have given the condition case to רבי ישמעאל if he allowed it, so his silence shows he forbids it

steps.title: Your question hits your own view too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רב זביד. Even by his own view, רבי עקיבא could have used the 'not firmly refused' case and he didn't.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, let him answer him with that case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב זביד's question proves too much. It is setting up the final answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד asked this same question about the 'not firmly refused' case (step 18), and it was answered in step 19, so he accepts that case fits רבי עקיבא. Yet רבי עקיבא didn't mention that case either. So his silence cannot prove that he disagrees with the condition case.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
let him answer him with that!
phrases.notes: 'That' is the slave who has not firmly refused, the case from step 17.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רב זביד's challenge in step 23
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that leaving a case out proves רבי עקיבא disagrees with it
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same argument would also disprove the 'not firmly refused' case, which רב זביד himself accepts

steps.title: רבי עקיבא gave one of two or three reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי עקיבא mentioned just one out of two or three valid cases. All of them can fit his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he said one out of two or three reasons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer. רבי עקיבא's twilight case was just one of several possible examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twilight case, the 'not firmly refused' case and the condition case can all fit רבי עקיבא. He named only one of them, which does not mean he rejects the others. So both רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי אילעאי can follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי עקיבא, who is strict about keeping an uncircumcised slave, may allow it in three cases: a slave bought at twilight, a slave who has not firmly refused, and a slave bought on condition not to be circumcised. He mentioned only one of them.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, חַד מִתְּרֵי וּתְלָת טַעְמֵי קָאָמַר.
phrases.english: Rather, he said one out of two or three reasons.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, חַד מִתְּרֵי וּתְלָת טַעְמֵי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final answer after the pushback in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Leaving cases out is not a rejection; the תנא named one of several valid cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's choice of the twilight case shows he forbids the other cases
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא gave one example out of two or three, so the other rulings can also fit his view

steps.title: A city that kept unwilling slaves for twelve months
steps.stepSummary: Three אמוראים discuss a city whose slaves refused מילה. The masters waited twelve months and then sold them to gentiles. The גמרא asks whose opinion this follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפי, רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא sat in the courtyard of רבי יצחק נפחא. They said: there was a city in ארץ ישראל whose slaves did not want to be circumcised. The owners put up with them for twelve months and then sold them to gentiles. Whose opinion did they follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story about slaves who refused מילה, then asks which תנא this practice follows. This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The masters did two things: they waited twelve months, and they kept the slaves in ארץ ישראל during that time. The question 'כמאן' asks which view allows this, since not every תנא agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: They put up with them / were patient with them
In line with whom? (whose opinion is this?)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi was sitting
and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha
in the courtyard of Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha,
and they were sitting and saying:
There was one city in the Land of Israel
whose slaves did not want to be circumcised,

phrases.aramaic: וְגִלְגְּלוּ עִמָּהֶם עַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: and they put up with them for up to twelve months,
and then they sold them to gentiles.
phrases.notes: 'They' here means the slaves' owners.

phrases.english: In line with whose opinion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבי עקיבא discussion to a real case about keeping uncircumcised slaves.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא allows keeping an uncircumcised slave in ארץ ישראל for twelve months before selling him.

steps.title: The ברייתא that allows twelve months
steps.stepSummary: The city followed the first opinion of a ברייתא: a master is patient for twelve months, and then sells the slave to gentiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: if someone buys a slave from a gentile and the slave does not want to be circumcised, the master puts up with him for up to twelve months. If he still has not been circumcised, the master sells him to gentiles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא whose ruling matches exactly what the city did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the same two parts as the story: twelve months of patience, then selling to gentiles. This shows the city's practice has a source in a תנא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from the time of the משנה

phrases.english: It is like this tanna,
as it is taught in a baraita:
One who buys a slave from a gentile
and the slave did not want to be circumcised,

phrases.aramaic: מְגַלְגֵּל עִמּוֹ עַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: the master puts up with him for up to twelve months.
If he still was not circumcised,
he then sells him to gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'כמאן' question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The city followed the first תנא of the ברייתא, who allows twelve months of patience and then a sale to gentiles.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר forbids keeping him in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagrees: such a slave may not stay in ארץ ישראל because he ruins pure items. In a border town he may not stay at all, in case he passes on secrets to the enemy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: we do not let him stay in ארץ ישראל, because of the loss of pure items. And in a city near the border we do not let him stay at all, in case he hears something and goes and tells his fellow gentile.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second opinion that disagrees with the first. This explains why the גמרא needed to ask 'כמאן': the city did not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives two worries. Anywhere in ארץ ישראל, the slave can make pure items impure, because he is still treated like a gentile. In a border town the worry is security: he might leak secrets to the enemy, so he may not be kept there even for a short time.
steps.whatToRemember: The city's practice of waiting twelve months in ארץ ישראל follows the first תנא, not רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
We do not let him stay in the Land of Israel,
because of the loss of ritually pure items.
phrases.notes: While uncircumcised he counts like a gentile, so pure food he touches becomes impure.

phrases.english: And in a city near the border
we do not let him stay at all,
in case he hears some secret matter
and goes and tells it to his fellow gentile.
phrases.notes: He means a gentile on the enemy's side of the border.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view within the same ברייתא, showing why the city's practice fits only the first תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An uncircumcised slave may not be kept in ארץ ישראל because of pure items, and not at all in a border town because of security.

steps.title: Why converts suffer: they did not keep the seven Noahide laws
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: רבי חנניא son of רבן גמליאל says converts today suffer because, before converting, they did not keep שבע מצוות בני נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי חנניא son of רבן גמליאל says: why are converts nowadays oppressed, with hardships coming upon them? Because they did not keep the seven commandments of the children of נח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about גרים. It quotes a ברייתא that asks why converts suffer, and gives a first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנניא holds that converts are punished now for what they failed to do as gentiles. Before converting, they were obligated in שבע מצוות בני נח and did not keep them.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven commandments binding on all non-Jews

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Chananya, son of Rabban Gamliel, says:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה גֵּרִים בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה מְעוּנִּין,
phrases.english: Why are converts at the present time oppressed,
and hardships come upon them?

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא קִיְּימוּ שֶׁבַע מִצְוֹת בְּנֵי נֹחַ.
phrases.english: Because they did not keep the seven commandments of the children of Noah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from slaves who refuse מילה to a new ברייתא about converts in general.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Converts suffer because they did not keep שבע מצוות בני נח before converting.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: a convert is like a newborn, so the reason is different
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rejects the first reason, because a convert is like a newborn baby with a clean slate. Instead, converts suffer because they are not expert in the fine details of מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: a person who converted is like a newborn child. So why do they suffer? Because they are not as expert in the fine details of the מצוות as a born Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי pushes back on רבי חנניא's reason and offers a different one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a convert is like a newborn, his past as a gentile cannot be the cause of his suffering now. רבי יוסי moves the cause to the present: converts lack expertise in the details of מצוות, so they often slip up by mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: The fine details of the commandments

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not denying that converts suffer. He agrees they do and only rejects the reason that it is for their past as gentiles.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
A convert who converted is like a child who was just born.
phrases.notes: So he is not punished for anything he did before converting.

phrases.english: Rather, why are they oppressed?
Because they are not expert
in the fine details of the commandments like a born Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי חנניא's reason and offers a new one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that converts are punished for sins from before their conversion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A convert is like a newborn, so his past cannot be held against him.

steps.title: אבא חנן: they serve from fear, not love
steps.stepSummary: אבא חנן, in the name of רבי אלעזר, says converts suffer because they keep מצוות out of fear rather than love.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא חנן says in the name of רבי אלעזר: because they do not act out of love, only out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion gives another reason why converts suffer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason looks at the converts' motive, not their past or their knowledge. They keep מצוות out of fear of punishment, not out of love of הקב"ה.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא חָנָן אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Abba Chanan says in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
Because they do not act out of love,
but only out of fear.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא חָנָן אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third reason after רבי יוסי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Converts suffer because they keep מצוות out of fear and not out of love.

steps.title: אחרים: they waited too long to convert
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say converts suffer because they delayed before coming under the wings of the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: because they held themselves back from entering under the wings of the שכינה.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth opinion gives yet another reason: converts are punished for not converting sooner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the fault is the delay itself. They knew they could join the Jewish people and waited, and that waiting brings hardship.

keyTerms.meaning: The wings of the Divine Presence

phrases.english: Others say:
Because they held themselves back
from entering under the wings of the Divine Presence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth reason to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Converts suffer because they delayed their conversion.

steps.title: The פסוק from רות about coming under His wings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו (or רבי חנינא) brings a פסוק from רות to support the view of אחרים that one should not delay converting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said, and some say it was רבי חנינא: what is the source? 'May ה׳ repay your deeds, and may your reward be complete from ה׳, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take shelter.'
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא brings a פסוק to back up the last opinion, that converts are judged for how quickly they came to join the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בועז blesses רות with a full reward because she came to shelter under ה׳'s wings. The phrase 'under His wings' matches 'the wings of the שכינה.' So a full reward is tied to coming without delay, and those who wait lose some of it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse (that teaches this)?

steps.whatToRemember: There are four reasons why converts suffer: their past as gentiles, lack of expertise, serving from fear, and delay in converting. The last reason is supported by the פסוק about רות coming under ה׳'s wings.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said, and some say it was Rabbi Chanina:
What is the verse for this?
'May the Lord repay your deeds,
and may your reward be complete
from the Lord, the God of Israel,
for you have come to take shelter, etc.'
phrases.notes: רות 2:12. The פסוק continues 'under His wings,' which matches 'the wings of the שכינה.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק supporting the view of אחרים in step 32.
steps.raayaObject: The view that converts are punished for delaying their conversion.
